recipes.name: Mini Southwestern Corn Pup Muffins with Fiesta Dipping Sauce
ingredients_raw: 4 hot dogs, cut into 1 inch pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Coat two 12 cup muffin tins with nonstick cooking spray or line with paper liners.

In a large bowl, stir together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, chili powder, cumin and garlic powder. Make a well in the center and pour in the milk, egg and oil. Stir until well blended, then gently stir in the cheese. Drop a smal spoonful of the batter into the bottom of each muffin cup. Place a piece of hot dog on top of this batter. Fill cups with enough additional batter to cover the hot dog pieces.

Bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven, or until muffins are lightly browned and spring back when lightly pressed. Cool slightly before removing from the muffin pans. Serve warm with the Fiesta Dipping Sauce.
To make the Fiesta Dipping Sauce, whisk together the sour cream, mayonnaise and taco seasoning mix until smooth. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Mini Southwestern Corn Pup Muffins with Fiesta Dipping Sauce
raw_recipe.description: This recipe is a great alternative to the fried corn dogs, and they taste just as good. Serve with the Fiesta Dipping Sauce recipe provided, or use your favorite corn dog condiments.

review.reviewBody: Very tasty, quick, and easy recipe. Kids and adults love it. I made only one change, I used dry taco seasoning mix instead of chili powder. Only suggestion I have is I made batches with both regular cupcake pans and mini cupcake pans. The regular sized ones came out slightly harder to eat, and stuck heavily to the cupcake wrappers I used. This was quite irritating when trying to eat them. Also, there was almost too much cornbread to hot dog ratio.(cut each dog into 1/4 pieces) On the other hand, the smaller Mini ones I made with my nonstick mini pan, I cooked a few minutes less, in these I used 1/8 of a hotdog pieces, and it worked perfect. They were so yummy, everyone ate these and left the big ones after tasting both. Perfect hotdog-corn mixture ratio. They weren't as floppy as the big ones.Fun to eat! I will definitely make these again, but from now on will use the mini cupcake pans only.

I used a "flax egg" instead of a regular egg since I was out (1 T ground flax seed & 1 T water) and less sugar than called for (~1//4 cup). It still turned out great and my kids liked them. I found the mini muffin tins took 10 minutes to cook and the regular muffin tins took almost 15. We just dipped ours in ketchup.

I truly have a special place in my heart for corndogs. These little guys are FANTASTIC!! I used 3 veggie hotdogs for 24 mini muffins. I cut each hotdog into 8 equal pieces. Using a small cookie scoop, I put a full scoop into each well of my silicone mini muffin pan, placed a hotdog chunk into each one, and topped them off with about 1 teaspoon of batter. I added 2 teaspoons of sugar to the dipping sauce, decreased the taco seasoning to 1 tablespoon, and added 1 tablespoon of milk to make it taste like Taco Bell's Santa Fe sauce (the sauce they so cruelly discontinued!). SO GOOD!!!

I didn't have any Monterey Jack cheese so I used some sharp cheddar instead. I made mine in mini muffin pans (and since the recipe has the word mini in the title I assume that's how they were meant to be made). I only needed to bake mine for 8 minutes but that's possibly because my oven runs a little hot. I haven't tried the dipping sauce and I'm not sure if I will since the muffins taste pretty good just by themselves. I think they have just the right amount of spices in them. I'll definitely keep this recipe in mind for the next time I want to do something a little different with hot dogs.

. Pretty good, but no magic. True, I didn't make the sauce. 'Only change to muffins was reducing the cumin to 3/4t. I couldn't detect much southwestern, if any; which, I suppose, was fine, but it surprised me. The cheese wasn't evident either. I wonder if topping on the muffins before baking would be better. A hit of mustard may be a good addition; chopped jalapenos/onions. Twelve fullsize muffins. Oh, decreased sugar to 1/4c & it wasn't too much or too little. I'm thinking one more doggie, too. Four hot dogs probably means a half pound, but OM wieners come ten per package - so five would be a half pound. I'm weird about numbers sometimes. I know. ;)

What an excellent way to use up some unwanted hot dogs. I made these into 12 regular muffins, chopped the hotdogs into pieces and used pepperjack cheese for some added kick. I doubled the cheese, but also used a course grate. Hubby liked them topped with mustard and I thought they were great plain.

So yummy! The spice was mild enough for my kids, and they thought they were fantastic. I used a mini-muffin pan as well (they baked up in 7 minutes). I stuck lollipop sticks from the craft store in them per my 6 yr old request, "to make them like a real corn dog". I didn't make the sauce, as the kiddos just wanted to dip it in ketchup. Definitely going in circulation. Thanks for the lovely recipe!

We make these in a mini-muffin pan. The perfect hot dog/bread ratio for us is 1/8 of a normal sized hot dog. The batter fits perfectly into 36 mini muffins. The only change we make is to double the cheese. The sauce is good - however if you let it sit over night it becomes great! My husband eats these cold the next day.

Very nice. I made them as mini muffins. The cornbread, with about 2/3 the sugar, was excellent. They were good with hotdogs but would be even better with something a bit spicier. They would also be good vegetarian mini muffins with some jalapeno and corn or some other filling. I didn’t make the sauce.

I cheated and used Jiffy Corn Muffin mix as well, 2 boxes. I also made this a southwest type mix by adding 2 packages of taco seasoning to the mix. For the hot dogs I used the smoked little weenies and cut them in half. I poured the batter in mini muffin pans. I took them to our football tailgate this past week-end, and everybody raved about them. I came back empy handed too!

this was exceptionally yummy - I cut the hot dogs up small so my toddler could eat it too and I increased the oil to 1/4 cup - I had to increase the baking time about 5 minutes but the end result was yummy - nothing stuck to the paper liner - I would mix the sauce first before starting on everything else though, really yummy
Definitely lacked some flavor and dry. Made as directed and made no ingredient subs. The only thing I did do differently was to make 24 mini muffins and bake 8-10 minutes. Not sure I’d make again.
Instead of hotdogs I used breakfast sausage (maple flavored) cut in small pieces, delicious!
The muffins are so good you do not even need the dipping sauce.
very good! I used Jiffy mix. Ate them with ketchup and mustard. The dipping sauce sounds great but, I didn't have any sour cream. I will make these again for sure!

the recipe was not quite enough to fill 24 regular muffin tins. When I make it again I will definitely make maybe 18 and cut the hotdogs pieces smaller so there's more per muffin. I did not try the sauce since these will be packed as kids lunches. They taste great though and I really love the slightly spicy taste. I think with slight modifications these will be 5 star.

I did not try the sauce since these will be packed as kids lunches. They taste great though and I really love the slightly spicy taste. I think with slight modifications these will be 5 star.

Really great recipe...thank you. I did make a few changes as I didn't have the cheese so I omitted it but I am sure they would have been even better with the cheese. I am also GF so instead of flour I used 1/2 cup Arnels GF flour and 1/2 cup Cassava flour. I also used taco seasoning as another rater suggested.

Super yummy and great lunch idea for kids! I used Jiffy mix in place of cornmeal because it was all I had on hand. Otherwise I stuck to the recipe, cooking the muffins an additional 2-3 minutes. The batter only made 14 muffins for me. Next time I will cut the hot dogs up into small pieces and mix throughout the batter.

WOW! I thought my kids would love these for an easy, quick after school snack... But only made the sauce for my husband. Now I'm thinking there won't be any left by the time the kids get off the bus! I only adjusted the amount of chili powder to half of what was called for and these are SO DELICIOUS!
